title: check: no cap on keys/signature blocks; quadratic ssh-keygen runs
description:
There is no cap on keys per person file or signature blocks per .sig, so one person file makes every check (sync, keys, query, status) run quadratically many ssh-keygen processes.

Where (HEAD 4237c43): verify_person at git-vouch:1003-1019 calls _signer (934-938) for every block in the .sig. _signer runs one `ssh-keygen -Y verify` per candidate key until one matches. split_signatures (900-911) and _person (739) accept any count within the 64 KiB file cap. verify_person runs at least twice per person-file version (origin at 1530, warning loop at 1719), and every version in history is re-judged on every run.

Measured (scratchpad a1/caps.sh, about 5 ms per ssh-keygen verify): a person file with N keys whose .sig holds N valid blocks signed in reverse key order takes 4.4 s for N=20 and 10.6 s for N=40. 64 KiB holds about 370 key entries and about 208 blocks, which is about 55k verifies per verify_person call. That is about 4.5 minutes, about 9 minutes per check, for each such version, permanently. A self-registered person with no tier can submit it, and every later edit adds another version. patatt runs `git vouch keys` per patch check, so b4 inherits the delay.

This is separate from vouch-xlha.3 (re-verification at honest scale): a memo does not bound N×B.

Fix: constraints, not mechanisms. Cap keys per person file (e.g. 16; kernel.org issues a main and a backup token) and blocks per .sig (no more than the number of current keys, and e.g. 4), and report a problem above either cap. DESIGN.md "Input is untrusted" should name the caps next to the 64 KiB one.
notes: core-perf: fixed in working tree (uncommitted). check on synthetic 600-person registry (1,378 commits, 150 key rotations, --no-ff merges): 193.4 s before, 14.6 s after, identical output; git runs per check ~9,600 -> 11, ssh-keygen 1,948 (one per distinct signature). Caps: MAX_KEYS=16 per person file (retired included), MAX_SIGNATURES=4 per .sig.
close_reason: Caps: at most 16 current keys per person file (retired keys uncapped beyond 64 KiB, open question for Mark), at most 4 blocks per .sig. Tests: test_more_than_sixteen_current_keys_refused, test_more_than_four_signature_blocks_refused
